issues.legal_issue: A killing committed during a sudden fight without premeditation, in circumstances satisfying the requirements of the sudden-fight exception, is culpable homicide not amounting to murder where the offender had knowledge that the injuries were likely to cause death.
material_facts: The accused and the deceased became involved in a sudden quarrel after the deceased objected to the accused grazing buffaloes in the deceased’s field.
There was no prior deliberation or premeditation to fight.
During the altercation, the accused struck the deceased’s head with an axe, causing six head injuries and death.
The weapon and the injuries to the head supported attributing knowledge that the injuries were likely to cause death.
issues.conclusion: The conviction for murder was modified to a conviction for culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304 Part II IPC because the killing fell within Exception 4 to Section 300 IPC.
issues.legal_principle: Exception 4 to Section 300 IPC applies where death is caused without premeditation, in a sudden fight, without the offender taking undue advantage or acting cruelly or unusually, and in a fight with the person killed. Where the exception applies but the offender had knowledge that the injuries were likely to cause death, the offence is punishable under Section 304 Part II IPC.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and sudden_fight and no_premeditation and fight_with_deceased and no_undue_advantage_or_cruel_conduct and knowledge_injuries_likely_fatal

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The matter is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.sudden_fight: The accused and the deceased became involved in a fight that arose suddenly.
predicates.no_premeditation: The accused had not deliberated or determined in advance to fight or kill the deceased.
predicates.fight_with_deceased: The sudden fight was between the accused and the person who died.
predicates.no_undue_advantage_or_cruel_conduct: The accused did not take undue advantage or act cruelly or unusually during the fight.
predicates.knowledge_injuries_likely_fatal: The accused inflicted injuries in circumstances showing knowledge that they were likely to cause death.

issues.definition: When a criminal conviction appeal concerns a killing in a sudden, unpremeditated fight with the deceased, and the accused neither took undue advantage nor acted cruelly or unusually but knew the injuries were likely to cause death, the conviction is for culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

issues.legal_issue: The enhanced offence based on a victim’s Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe status requires evidence that the offence was committed on the ground of that status, and is not established merely by the victim’s status or a caste reference during an unrelated quarrel.
material_facts: The deceased belonged to a Scheduled Caste.
The accused referred to the deceased’s caste during a wordy altercation that arose because the deceased objected to the accused grazing buffaloes in the deceased’s field.
The evidence did not establish that the offence was committed only because the deceased belonged to a Scheduled Caste.
issues.conclusion: The conviction under Section 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act was set aside, and the accused was acquitted of that charge.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, as applied in Dinesh alias Buddha v. State of Rajasthan (2006) 3 SCC 771, requires the offence to have been committed against the victim on the ground that the victim was a member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe. Proof of the victim’s status alone is insufficient.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The matter is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.victim_is_member_of_protected_caste_or_t: The person against whom the offence was committed belonged to a protected caste or tribe.
predicates.no_evidence_offence_committed_on_status_: The evidence did not establish that the accused committed the offence because the victim belonged to that caste or tribe.

issues.definition: If a criminal conviction appeal concerns a victim who belonged to a protected caste or tribe but the evidence does not establish that the offence was committed on that ground, the conviction under the caste-atrocity offence is set aside and the accused is acquitted of that charge.

issues.legal_issue: After a conviction is reduced to culpable homicide not amounting to murder, the sentence may be limited to the period already served when the court considers the circumstances and the accused has already served a substantial period in custody.
material_facts: The conviction for murder was modified to culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
The accused had served more than thirteen years in prison by the time of the Supreme Court’s decision.
The Court considered the facts and circumstances of the case in determining the sentence.
issues.conclusion: The sentence for culpable homicide not amounting to murder was imprisonment for the period already undergone, and the accused was ordered released if not required in another case.
issues.legal_principle: The Court imposed a sentence for the modified conviction after considering the facts and circumstances and the period of imprisonment already served; no earlier case or separate sentencing provision was cited for this determination.

predicates.criminal_appeal: The matter is a criminal appeal in which the court reviews the conviction and sentence.
predicates.conviction_modified_to_culpable_homicide: The court has modified the conviction to culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
predicates.substantial_period_already_served: The accused had already served a substantial period of imprisonment when the court determined the sentence.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal results in a conviction for culpable homicide not amounting to murder and the accused has already served a substantial period in prison, the sentence may be limited to the period already served.
